If your Apple CarPlay connection suddenly drops while you're driving, the problem may not lie with your iPhone, the cable, or the car itself.

It might instead be caused by radio wave interference.

An Axios report once detailed a strange phenomenon in Boston: drivers would lose their CarPlay or Android Auto connection when passing through certain locations. Similar "signal dead zones" likely exist in other cities too, just that no one may have complained about them.

A CarPlay head unit cannot independently handle GPS navigation. It maintains a direct connection with your iPhone via Bluetooth or Wi-Fi and then mirrors a display; the content on that display relies on the phone's internet and GPS satellite connection. When the wireless connection between the head unit and the phone is interfered with, navigation fails and the connection may also drop.

Comment by Mainframe received the most likes

In Grapevine, Texas, I have a specific location on a stretch of road between an oil storage facility and a nursing home that kills all wireless CarPlay systems. I've tried several cars, including ones with factory-installed wireless CarPlay, ones with wireless CarPlay adapters, and aftermarket audio systems, and they all freeze on this stretch. Some systems recover on their own after being interfered with, some don't. Even the latest Mercedes-Benz electric vehicle has this problem.

I've only encountered this situation a handful of times in the past decade.

Experts point out that nearby radio sources, particularly signals on the 2.4GHz frequency band, could be the source of interference. In the case of Boston, it has been speculated to include point-to-point microwave links, broadcast antennas, or unlicensed transmitters.

The key point is, if you frequently lose your CarPlay connection in the same location, you may be driving through an invisible zone of radio wave interference. This problem may not be solvable, but knowing the cause can save you a lot of time, so you don't have to keep searching for the reason or scheduling unnecessary repair services.
